core_obligations: Import the finite pushforward equivalence for i.
Verify the pseudo-coherence hypothesis on the chart P over S.
Specialize the composition law to id_P to exchange relative and absolute notions.

proof_roadmap.step: Pushforward equivalence via the finite-map theorem.
Composition law at the smooth chart plus the flat-finitely-presented perfectness input.

difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram with i : X -> P a closed immersion and P -> S flat locally of finite presentation, and E in D(O_X), the lemma identifies three conditions: E m-pseudo-coherent relative to S; Ri_* E m-pseudo-coherent relative to S; Ri_* E m-pseudo-coherent (absolutely) on P. The retained proof is written: (1) iff (2) is the finite-morphism pushforward theorem (chapter lemma finite-morphism-relative-pseudo-coherence — this same wave's L16133, sequenced together); (2) iff (3) applies the composition law (chapter lemma composition-relative-pseudo-coherent — collected last wave as L16115) to the identity of P, whose hypothesis that O_P be pseudo-coherent relative to S is verified from More on Algebra, lemma flat-finite-presentation-perfect (flat finitely presented maps are perfect, hence pseudo-coherent) plus the dictionary between relative pseudo-coherence of the structure sheaf and pseudo-coherence of the morphism. Retained author proof at lines 17294-17306.
